Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.workspace

Class WorkspaceRegistry

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.workspace.WorkspaceRegistry
public final class WorkspaceRegistry extends Object
The native 3D desktop's workspace bookkeeping: the pure mapping from a window id to "is this window shown right now", built on the desktop-agnostic WorkspaceModel the 2D/Swing desktop already uses.

The registry holds no Java 3D and no Swing. A window is registered under a stable string id together with a WorkspaceRegistry.VisibilitySink — in the live desktop that sink is frame3d::setVisible, so this class stays headless-testable while the WorkspacePlugin keeps only the scene-graph glue. The rule is a single sentence: a registered window is visible exactly when it sits on the current workspace. Every mutator re-applies that rule, so a switch can never leave a window shown on two workspaces or hidden on the one being entered.

Workspaces here are a partition of the windows of the single StandardAppContainer, not multiple app containers. The multi-container plumbing in GlassySceneManager was evaluated and rejected: SceneControl.setCurrentAppContainer deliberately does not add the container to the scene graph (its own comment says the caller must), AppContainer.setEnabled only flips a flag, lazily-created container slots can still be null when setCurrentAppContainer iterates them, and — decisively — StandardAppContainer.initialize() registers global Frame3D listeners (a to-front handler that migrates the frame into that container's main layout) whose own comment warns that instantiating the container more than once duplicates those actions. A second workspace container would therefore steal frames back into the first.

Indexes wrap and counts clamp exactly as WorkspaceModel defines, so no call here can select a workspace that does not exist.

  • Method Details

    • windowId

      public static String windowId(String name, int identityHash)
      The stable window id for a scene-graph frame: its name, made unique by an identity hash so two instances of the same app never collide. The 2D desktop can key its model on Desktop2DWindow.getAppName() because that is already unique among open windows; a Frame3D name is not, so the caller passes System.identityHashCode(frame). Pure, so it is testable without constructing any Java 3D object.

    • count

      public int count()
      How many workspaces there are.

    • current

      public int current()
      The index of the workspace currently shown.

    • register

      public boolean register(String windowId, WorkspaceRegistry.VisibilitySink sink)
      Registers windowId on the current workspace and shows it. A null or empty id, or a null sink, is ignored and returns false; re-registering the same id replaces the sink and re-assigns the window to the current workspace.

    • unregister

      public boolean unregister(String windowId)
      Forgets windowId (its window closed). Returns true when it was registered. The sink is dropped without being called: the window that owned it no longer exists, so there is nothing to hide.

    • switchTo

      public int switchTo(int index)
      Shows the workspace at index (wrapped) and reconciles every registered window against it. Returns the new current index.

    • next

      public int next()
      Shows the next workspace, wrapping to the first. Returns its index.

    • previous

      public int previous()
      Shows the previous workspace, wrapping to the last. Returns its index.

    • moveTo

      public void moveTo(String windowId, int index)
      Moves windowId to the workspace at index (wrapped) and reconciles visibility — so moving a window to another workspace hides it from this one, exactly as the 2D desktop's "move to workspace" does. Unknown or null ids are ignored.

    • workspaceOf

      public int workspaceOf(String windowId)
      The workspace windowId is on, or -1 when it is not registered.

    • isOnCurrent

      public boolean isOnCurrent(String windowId)
      True when windowId is registered and shown on this workspace.

    • countOn

      public int countOn(int index)
      How many registered windows sit on the workspace at index.

    • windowIds

      public Set<String> windowIds()
      Every registered window id, in registration order. Never null.

    • windowCount

      public int windowCount()
      How many windows are registered in total.

    • applyVisibility

      public void applyVisibility()
      Re-applies the visibility rule to every registered window. Idempotent; a sink that throws is logged and skipped so the rest still reconcile.

    • releaseAll

      public void releaseAll()
      Shows every registered window and forgets them all — the shutdown path. A plugin that simply dropped its registry would leave the windows of every other workspace invisible with nothing left to show them again, so teardown must always restore the desktop to a single-workspace state first.

    • addListener

      public void addListener(WorkspaceRegistry.Listener listener)
      Adds a pager/observer. Duplicate additions are ignored.

    • removeListener

      public void removeListener(WorkspaceRegistry.Listener listener)
      Removes a pager/observer.
